Read every published prometheus-operator-dev package for Alpine 3.24 from the DHI Alpine repository: 24 builds, 0.92.1-r2 to the current 0.95.2-r3, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each installs one file, /usr/bin/prometheus-operator, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, and both architectures agree for every build. Its Go build information shows that 0.92.1-r2, 0.93.0-r0 and 0.93.1-r0 were built with Go 1.26.5, and every build from 0.93.1-r1 to 0.95.2-r3 with Go 1.26.6 to 1.26.11; golang.org/x/net is 0.56.0 or later in every build. The range ends at 0.93.1-r1, the first build made with a fixed Go release.

Go 1.26.6 carries the fix as https://github.com/golang/go/commit/0e8a244fe52b1171937813a78f61e8a1075844dd, which is not in Go 1.26.5. The standard library is compiled into each Go program, so a build is fixed when it was built with Go 1.26.6 or later. Read every published prometheus-operator-fips-dev package for Alpine 3.24 from the DHI Alpine security repository, which requires authentication and is where the FIPS packages are published: 24 builds, 0.92.1-r2 to the current 0.95.2-r3, each for x86_64 and aarch64. Each installs one file, /usr/bin/prometheus-operator, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0, and both architectures agree for every build. Its Go build information shows that 0.92.1-r2, 0.93.0-r0 and 0.93.1-r0 were built with Go 1.26.5, and every build from 0.93.1-r1 to 0.95.2-r3 with Go 1.26.6 to 1.26.11; golang.org/x/net is 0.56.0 or later in every build. The range ends at 0.93.1-r1, the first build made with a fixed Go release.

The Go standard library carries its own copy of that package, which the net package's resolver reaches through LookupCNAME. Go 1.26.6 carries the fix as https://github.com/golang/go/commit/0e8a244fe52b1171937813a78f61e8a1075844dd on release-branch.go1.26, which is not in Go 1.26.5. Checked /usr/bin/trivy, the only file in every published trivy-dev package in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository (0.69.1-r0 to 0.74.0-r12, 38 builds each on x86_64 and aarch64), each verified against the repository index checksum, reading its Go build information (go version -m) and its Go symbol table (go tool nm function entries). Each is a statically linked Go program for Linux, built with CGO_ENABLED=0. The Go toolchain is 1.25.7 in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r0, 1.26.1 to 1.26.5 in 0.69.3-r1 to 0.73.0-r0, and 1.26.6 to 1.26.10 from 0.73.0-r2 on; both architectures agree for every build. The resolver function the advisory lists, net.(*Resolver).LookupCNAME, is in the symbol table of every build. The standard library's copy in the Go 1.25 builds has no SVCB code: a search of the raw bytes of /usr/bin/trivy finds the name SVCBResource in 0.69.3-r1, the first Go 1.26 build, and none in 0.69.1-r0, 0.69.2-r0 or 0.69.3-r0, on both architectures. golang.org/x/net is 0.50.0 to 0.55.0 up to 0.71.2-r2 and 0.57.0 to 0.63.0 from 0.71.2-r3 on, but no function of the module's own golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage package is in the symbol table of any build, and the raw-byte search of 0.69.1-r0 to 0.69.3-r1 on both architectures finds no golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage name other than the standard library's vendored copy, which both searches do find. So the builds made with Go 1.26.1 to 1.26.5, 0.69.3-r1 to 0.73.0-r0, are affected, the earlier Go 1.25 builds are not, and 0.73.0-r2 is the first build made with Go 1.26.6; every later build keeps a fixed Go.

Go 1.26.6 fixes the copy of golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage vendored into the standard library (used by the net package resolver), and golang.org/x/net v0.56.0 fixes the module (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5942, https://go.dev/cl/786345, https://go.dev/issue/79795, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/94pEornpRlI). This package is the Go 1.26 toolchain, and its version is the Go release it packages. In the published golang-1.26-dev packages for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository, amd64 and arm64, 1.26.5-0 lacks the fix while 1.26.6-0 and every later build ship /usr/lib/go/src/vendor/golang.org/x/net/dns/dnsmessage/svcb.go with the fix (each SVCB parameter value is checked against the remaining message before it is copied); their go command reports the Go release in the package version (go1.26.5 for 1.26.5-0, go1.26.6 for 1.26.6-0). Every published build below 1.26.6-0 (1.26.4-0 to 1.26.5-0) packages a Go release before 1.26.6, and every build from 1.26.6-0 to the current 1.26.11-18 packages 1.26.6 or later. The range ends at 1.26.6-0.
